<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|299}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=4|verse=5}}† And it came to passe on the morovv, that their princes, and Auncients, and Scribes vvere gathered into Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=6}}† and Annas the high priest, and Caiphas and Iohn, and Alexander, and as many as vvere of the priests stocke. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=7}}† And setting them in the middes, they asked: In vvhat povver or in vvhat name haue you done this? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=8}}† Then Peter replenished vvith the holy Ghost, said to them, Ye princes of the people & Auncients: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=9}}† If vve this day be examined for a good deede vpon an impotent man, in vvhat he hath been made whole, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=10}}† be it knovven to al you and to al the people of Israël, that in {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The name of IESVS. ''See Annot. Philip. 2,10''.}}∷ the name of {{sc|Iesvs}} Christ of Nazareth, vvhom you did crucifie, vvhom God hath raised from the dead, in this same this man standeth before you vvhole. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=11}}† This is {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 117, 22.''}}* ''the stone that vvas reiected of you the builders: vvhich is made into the head of the corner''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=12}}† and there is not saluation in any other. for neither is there any other name vnder heauen giuen to men, vvherein vve must be saued. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Apostles constancie, learning and vvisdom after the comming of the Holy Ghost, being but idiotes, that is, simple vnlettered men and timorous before.}}∷ And seeing Peters constancie and Iohns, vnderstanding that they vvere men vnlettered, and of the vulgar sort, they marueled, and they knew them that they had been vvith {{sc|Iesvs}}: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=14}}† seeing the man also that had been cured, standing vvith them, they could say nothing to the contrarie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=15}}† But they commaunded them to goe aside forth out of the councel: and they conferred together, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=16}}† saying, VVhat shal vve doe to these men? for a notorious signe in deede hath been done by them, to al the inhabitants of Hierusalem: it is manifest, and vve can not denie it. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=17}}† But that it be no further spred abrode among the people, let vs threaten them, that they speake no more in this name to any man. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† And calling them, they charged them that they should not speake at al, nor teache in the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† But Peter and Iohn ansvvering, said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Their constancie and courage after their confirmation, being so weake before. And if any Magistrate commaund against God, that is to say, forbid Catholike Christian men to preach or serue God, this same must be their answer, though they be vvhipped and killed for their labour. ''See c. 5. v. 29''.}}∷ If it be iust in the sight of God, to heare you rather then God, iudge ye. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† for vve can not but speake the things vvhich vve haue seen and heard. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† But they threatening, dimissed them: not finding hovv they might punish them, for the people, because all glorified that vvhich had been done, in that vvhich vvas chaunced. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† For the man vvas more then fourtie yeres old, in vvhom that signe of health had been vvrought.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† And being dimissed they came to theirs, and shevved al that the cheefe priests and Auncients had said to them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† VVho hauing heard it, with one accord lifted vp their voice to<noinclude>{{rh||Pp ij|God,}}</noinclude>
